Check filterByModel() against NONMEM's own account of the data

verifyFilterByModel.Rd

Every NONMEM run prints how many records, subjects and observations it read once the $DATA record had been applied. Those three numbers are an independent check on filterByModel(): they come from NONMEM, not from a reading of the control stream, so they catch a filter that is wrong in the same way your own reading of $DATA is wrong.

It needs nothing but artefacts already on disk - the control stream, its .lst, and the data file - and never re-runs anything.

Usage

verifyFilterByModel(
  modFile,
  data = NULL,
  lstFile = NULL,
  idVar = "ID",
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

modFile

Path to the control stream.

data

The data set as a data frame. Optional: when absent the $DATA record is resolved relative to modFile and read.

lstFile

Path to the run's .lst. Optional: <model>.lst, .res, .out and NM_run1/psn.lst are tried in turn.

idVar

Name of the subject column, for the subject count.

quiet

Suppress the progress messages from filterByModel().

Value

A length-1 logical, usable directly in an if, with attributes:

  • checks - a data frame of CHECK, FILTERED, NONMEM, DIFF and PASS, one row per comparison.

  • informative - FALSE when the $DATA record removed nothing, so the comparison could not have failed.

  • removed - how many records the $DATA record removed, measured against NONMEM's own count (rawRows minus NO. OF DATA RECS) and so independent of what filterByModel() did. On a failing check it will not reconcile with the filtered count, which is the point.

  • rawRows - rows in the data set as read, before filtering.

  • obsBasis - "MDV", "EVID" or "NONE".

Details

The observation count follows NONMEM: records with MDV == 0, or EVID == 0 where the data set carries no MDV column.

The .lst describes the model NONMEM read, which is not always the model on disk. Where its echoed $INPUT or $DATA filter clauses disagree with modFile, the counts no longer describe it and the comparison is noise, so this warns. Columns are matched by position, so a changed $INPUT matters even when the names are all still there.

A $DATA record that removes nothing agrees with the .lst whatever filterByModel() does. That is reported as attr(., "informative") rather than hidden, because such a result is not evidence of anything.

See also

filterByModel() for the filtering itself, and verifyParamFunction(), which does the same job for a generated parameter function.

Examples

modFile <- system.file("extdata", "SimVal/run7.mod", package = "PMXForest")
v <- verifyFilterByModel(modFile, quiet = TRUE)
v
#> PASS - verifyFilterByModel: 3/3 check(s) (35131 record(s) removed)
#>         CHECK FILTERED NONMEM DIFF PASS
#>       RECORDS    33885  33885    0 TRUE
#>      SUBJECTS      754    754    0 TRUE
#>  OBSERVATIONS     6284   6284    0 TRUE
if (v) message("filterByModel() reproduced the run")
#> filterByModel() reproduced the run
attr(v, "checks")
#>          CHECK FILTERED NONMEM DIFF PASS
#> 1      RECORDS    33885  33885    0 TRUE
#> 2     SUBJECTS      754    754    0 TRUE
#> 3 OBSERVATIONS     6284   6284    0 TRUE
